title: Rigorix Policy & Configuration Model v1
description: v1 (2026-09-07) — grounded in rigorix-oss engine code (code is truth): sequence-policy rules from engine/src/sequence_policy/domain/rule.rs + config.rs (SequenceRule, StepPredicate, ParamPredicate, HistoryPredicate, RuleAction, SequencePolicyConfig, SafetyCaps) and the root rigorix.toml surface from engine/src/configuration/domain/config.rs (permission_mode, audit HMAC knobs). Root validates the OPERATOR-authored sequence-policy file (`[sequence_policy]` with `[[rules]]`, as consumed from .rigorix/sequence-policy.toml). The root config surface (rigorix.toml) is represented at $defs.rootConfigSurface for cross-tool alignment — permission_mode is a runtime-validated string (engine: Option<String>); known values documented. Enterprise policy_engine bundles must emit rule semantics in this shape (id/action/window/history/step predicates) — extension slots (approval policy, scope roles) are enterprise-only and land in the delta map. ADR-015: additive root `requirements` (StepRequirement/RequirementAction) + SafetyCaps `max_requirements_per_file` / `max_required_params_per_requirement`. ADR-017: additive root `preconditions` (dispatch-time authority checks) + `gating` (step-outcome gating), and `require_companion_step` on `[[requirements]]` (closes the ADR-015 companion-step non-goal).

fail_closed.description: Fail closed on config errors at plan time. Default true — a corrupt rule file must refuse the plan, never silently degrade.

rules.description: Ordered rule set (empty → no sequence gating).

requirements.description: R9/ADR-015: ordered operator-controlled step requirements (serde field on SequencePolicyConfig; additive and defaulted empty). Each matches planned steps via the frozen stepPredicate matcher and asserts obligations (attested identity and/or required parameter pointers), evaluated at plan time for every plan — independent of the (agent-authored) plan. Empty → no requirements.

preconditions.description: ADR-017 R1: ordered operator-authored dispatch-time preconditions ([[preconditions]] in .rigorix/preconditions.toml — operator-owned, never agent-writable). Each matches an about-to-dispatch step and runs an argv check; pass = dispatch, non-zero / timeout / spawn / trust-boundary / unarmed = refuse (fail closed). Empty → no preconditions (today's behavior).

gating.description: ADR-017 R2: step-outcome gating mode. Absent → today's behavior (dependents always released).

sequenceRule.description: One operator-authored sequence rule. Match requires steps[i] to appear before steps[i+1] in the evaluated ordered step list.

description.description: Why the rule exists (surfaced to approvers / audit summaries).

window.description: Max index gap between first and last matched step. Absent = adjacent pair (gap 1).

action.description: Action on match (serde lowercase). Default promote.

history.description: R7: optional cross-run predicate — fires only when the within-run steps match AND the signed execution history shows a prior action by the same principal within the window. Absent = pre-R7 within-run behavior.

stepPredicate.description: Matches a tool name (exact or glob) plus optional parameter predicates.

tool.description: Tool name — exact or glob, e.g. "registration_remove", "registration_*".

params.description: Optional parameter predicates; empty means any parameters. Default empty.

paramPredicate.description: JSON pointer into the step's parameter object plus a value predicate (exact | glob | regex | equals_step).

pointer.description: JSON pointer into step parameters, e.g. "/event_id".

kind.description: How value is compared (serde): exact/glob/regex use `value`; equals_step (R8/ADR-014) compares to an earlier matched step's pointer value via `step`.

value.description: Expected value string. REQUIRED for exact/glob/regex (a missing value is a fail-closed config error — never a silent empty match); unused and omitted for equals_step.

step.description: R8/ADR-014: for kind=equals_step, the index (into the rule's steps[]) of the EARLIER matched step whose `pointer` value must equal this one.

historyPredicate.description: R7 cross-run predicate: a prior, already-completed run in the signed audit trail contained a conflicting action by the same principal, minutes apart.

prior_node.description: Glob over prior executed node names, e.g. "remove_attendance" or "remove_*".

same_principal.description: true → only history actions whose principal equals the current run's principal satisfy the predicate. Current run with no principal → predicate cannot match (never a false denial).

window_secs.description: Look-back window (seconds) over the signed history.

effect_key.description: R8/ADR-014: when true, additionally require a prior run whose envelope `effect_key` (one-way keyed hash, domain-supplied) equals the current step's `/effect_key`. Absent/false = principal+node only. A prior envelope without an effect key never matches.

requirementAction.description: R9/ADR-015: action taken when a matched step fails a requirement (serde lowercase). `deny` refuses the plan before dispatch; `promote` sets requires_approval on the matched step (parameter obligations only — an unmet identity is always `deny`, never promotable). Default `deny`.

stepRequirement.description: R9/ADR-015: one operator-authored step requirement ([[requirements]] in .rigorix/sequence-policy.toml — same trust surface as rules; operator-owned, never plan data). `match` reuses the frozen stepPredicate matcher; at least one of require_identity / require_params / require_companion_step MUST be set (a no-op requirement is a fail-closed config error); require_params pointers MUST start with `/` and are checked for presence only — the operator names a pointer, the domain supplies its value, no domain semantics enter the engine. `equals_step` parameter predicates are invalid in `match` (there is no earlier matched step).

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. "payout-guard" (required; non-empty and unique per file).

name.description: Human-readable requirement name, surfaced to approvers / audit summaries (required — the engine has no serde default).

description.description: Why the requirement exists. Serde-defaulted to empty.

match.description: Selects the steps the requirement governs (same matcher as sequence rules: tool exact/glob + parameter predicates). Serde-renamed from the Rust `r#match` keyword to the operator key `match`.

require_identity.description: When true, the caller MUST present an attested identity (idp_token / local_principal). Unmet → refuse the plan (an unmet identity is never promotable). Default false.

require_params.description: JSON pointers (e.g. "/beneficiary") that MUST resolve to a present, non-null value in the matched step's parameters. Presence only; pointer NAMES may be recorded in findings, parameter VALUES never are (SpanPrivacy). Default empty.

action.description: Action for unmet parameter obligations (`deny` default | `promote`). Identity failures are always `deny` regardless of this value.

match.description: Predicate the plan MUST contain a step for (companion obligation).

require_companion_step.description: ADR-017 R3: the plan MUST contain a step matching this predicate (closes the ADR-015 companion-step non-goal). Unmet → the requirement's `action` (deny default | promote), with a requirement_findings[] entry.

safetyCaps.description: Engine safety caps bounding the rule engine (SequencePolicyConfig validation). Defaults: 100 rules / 8 step predicates / window 5 / 8 regex predicates / 604800s history look-back / 100 requirements / 16 required params per requirement.

max_requirements_per_file.description: R9/ADR-015: maximum number of [[requirements]] entries per config file (default 100).

max_required_params_per_requirement.description: R9/ADR-015: maximum required JSON pointers per requirement (default 16) — bounds the pointer-resolution work an operator config can impose on a plan.

rootConfigSurface.description: rigorix.toml knobs that affect policy/enforcement/audit (engine/src/configuration/domain/config.rs). NOT exhaustive — additive-extensible; unknown keys ignored. Enterprise policy_engine alignment uses this surface for cross-tool identity (permission_mode semantics live in each runtime's enforcement layer).

permission_mode.description: Runtime-validated string; documented value: "workspace_write". Enforcement-layer interpretation differs OSS vs enterprise (delta map).

audit_hmac_key.description: HMAC key signing each local envelope. Never commit live values.

precondition.description: ADR-017 R1: one operator-authored dispatch-time authority check ([[preconditions]] in .rigorix/preconditions.toml). `match` reuses the frozen stepPredicate matcher; `command` is an argv array (no shell, no interpolation) whose program must resolve outside the agent-writable workspace (trust boundary — a check the agent can edit is no check). `require_params` reuses ADR-015 presence-only semantics.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. "beneficiary-eligible" (required; non-empty and unique per file).

match.description: Selects the about-to-dispatch step the precondition gates (tool exact/glob + parameter predicates; same matcher as rules/requirements).

require_params.description: JSON pointers that MUST be present (non-null) in the matched step's declared parameters, checked BEFORE the command runs; absent → refuse (fail closed). Presence only — pointer NAMES, never values. Default empty.

command.description: argv array (no shell). command[0] is the check program — it must resolve outside the agent-writable workspace, else the step is refused (`error`).

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock timeout; expiry refuses the step (`error`). Default 5000.

failure.description: Action on a non-zero exit. v1: the only value is `deny` (refuse; the tool is never called).

capture_output.description: When true the check's stdout may be captured (truncated/redacted). Default false — stdout is never recorded.

require_immutable_check.description: ADR-017 (#986): when true, refuse the matched step if the resolved check program (or `authority_path`) is writable by the engine's effective UID. Default false — the boundary is path + hook; immutability is opt-in. Unreadable metadata fails closed.

authority_path.description: ADR-017 (#987): optional operator-declared authority artifact the check consults (e.g. the beneficiary file). The engine hashes it into `authority_digest` (never its contents) and, under `require_immutable_check`, refuses when it is writable.

gating.description: ADR-017 R2: step-outcome gating. When `release_dependents_on_failure` is false, a failed (or denied) step does not release its transitive dependents — they are marked Skipped and never dispatched.

release_dependents_on_failure.description: Default true = today's behavior (dependents always released). Set false so a failed step stops what depends on it.
